title: Choosing Between Arrays, Hashes, Sets, and Ranges
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of choosing between arrays, hashes, sets, and ranges in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply choosing between arrays, hashes, sets, and ranges in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to modeling domain-specific data and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Choosing Between Arrays, Hashes, Sets, and Ranges through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding choosing between arrays, hashes, sets, and ranges helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Choosing Between Arrays, Hashes, Sets, and Ranges helps you reason about ordered versus keyed data. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Ordered versus keyed data. Then connect it to Uniqueness requirements. The remaining syllabus points—Membership checks, Modeling domain-specific data—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: Choosing Between Arrays, Hashes, Sets, and Ranges
content_blocks.code:
require "set"
a = Set[1, 2, 3]
b = Set[3, 4]
p a & b

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports choosing between arrays, hashes, sets, and ranges. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.
